question: Can the exact Laguna- and Rizal-locality rows in the BMB 2019 Laguna Lake table be linked to their current PSA city and municipality codes without splitting the shared waterbody identity?
method: Rendered and visually reviewed page 3 of the DENR-BMB 2019 inland-wetlands PDF. Linked only the municipalities/cities printed in the Laguna and Rizal locality cells to the current PSA Region IV-A PSGC rows. Kept Laguna de Bay as one shared waterbody lead. The earlier crosswalk omitted the locality cells; this batch records the visually checked correction without rewriting the older hash-pinned crosswalk. Historical area is not used as a current measurement.

heldOutRow.disposition: Held for an NCR/L2 locality review; this L1 batch assigns only the Laguna and Rizal rows to CALABARZON codes. Do not omit the visible NCR localities from the national shared-water review.

limitations: The BMB inventory is historical and selected, not a complete current lake or municipality inventory. Its historical area value is not adopted as current measurement or geometry.
All six codes represent source-listed locality context around one shared Laguna de Bay identity; no physical sub-lakes are created or inferred.
The visible NCR locality row is explicitly held out of this CALABARZON batch for a separate L2 crosswalk to NCR PSA codes.
Administrative localities do not define lake extent, shorelines, municipal-water boundaries, coordinates, access, fishing grounds, safety, or current fish presence.
No species assertions, salinity, hazards, regulations, or public-app records are added.

decisions.decision: Preserve one canonical shared Laguna de Bay lead and add three Laguna city and three Rizal municipality localities from their respective BMB table rows, matched to PSA codes.

nextAction: Review the BMB NCR row for Laguna de Bay under the NCR/L2 denominator, then continue exact locality rows for other CALABARZON waterbodies without splitting shared-water identities.
